name: broadleaf tree (lobed leaf-cluster crown, jp_city forest kit prototype)
label: jp-forest-proto/tree-t3x4
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (4/4)

answer.evidence: The crown is a large rounded leaf mass. Its width profile widens from 12 px at row 12 to 47 px at rows 27-29, then narrows to 18 px at row 47, so it reads as a domed volume. The lit, lighter yellow-green patches on the upper rows 12-26 read as the sunlit top surface seen from above. There is no hard front-edge line. The darker leaf clusters and outline on rows 40-46 act as underside shadow and the front mass. The trunk below is a vertical south face about 6 px wide on rows 47-62, with a small ground shadow at the base. The crown's top is implied by shading rather than drawn with an explicit edge line, so the evidence is moderate.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 18 distinct colours against 427 and 567 in the references, and 13 colours per tile against about 108. Its canopy reads as roughly 4 green steps with dithered clumps, but the clumps are small and tight, with little highlight variety. Compared with the references' bright, many-toned leaf clusters with distinct lobes, it looks darker, flatter and more muddy. The trunk is a thin, simple column with 2-3 browns and no root flare, branch structure showing through the crown, or bark grain, whereas both references have forked branches, roots and bark texture. Outlines are tinted dark green with no neutral edge pixels (0% neutral), which is acceptable. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so it is not flat, but the shading is shallow and the density is much lower than every reference.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a lobed crown with a thin trunk. Its dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline is dark green beside the leaves and fits the standard. It has no flat-fill blocks (0%) and some clumped mottling in the crown. It falls well short of the references on richness: 18 distinct colours against 427 and 567, and 13 colours per tile against 108 and 109. By eye the crown has about 4 green steps, and they are muddy, low-contrast clusters, with no bright highlight leaf clumps like the references' 5-6 steps. The trunk is a plain, narrow, nearly flat brown column with no root flare, branch structure or bark grain. The references show crisp individual leaf clumps, visible branches through the canopy, and a flared root base. The candidate looks thinner and flatter than both, so it is much lower in density and shading depth.
